answer: To secure an agent economy, nodes anchor cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs to a consensus ridge. Minting identities requires staking that scales exponentially (e.g. 2^n cost) per coordinated entity. When a Sybil swarm flashes across the network like a rogue comet, this steep curve enforces exponential capital exhaustion, burning their saffron stake reserves and making multi-identity attacks computationally and economically ruinous.
